findings.title: PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG entry omits required anti-overclaiming fields
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md Anti-Overclaiming Contract requires every conclusion to state: (1) what is strictly proven, (2) what is only implemented, (3) what is still assumed, (4) what would make the claim false. The Fix Attempt entry added in commit 31e142a provides a Verification section with '-> PASS' for pytest and node runs, and a Notes section disclaiming acceptance-grade status, but does not enumerate what is assumed or what would falsify the claim. This creates a gap in the required four-part proof protocol, even for a maintenance slice.
findings.suggested_fix: Append two items to the Notes section: (3) what is assumed — e.g., 'Assumes registry file on disk matches committed JSON; assumes test environment CONFIG_DIR resolves to repo root'; (4) what would make this false — e.g., 'A test run against a stale or differently-pathed config file would silently pass without validating the deployed artifact.'
evidence: CLAUDE.md §Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'Before any conclusion, state: 1. what is strictly proven 2. what is only implemented 3. what is still assumed 4. what would make the claim false'

PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md commit 31e142a adds entry titled 'Fix Attempt — Template Registry Coupling And Bundle Contract Validation' with Verification showing '-> PASS' but Notes section contains only two items (scope disclaimer and no-browser-run rationale), omitting the 'what is assumed' and 'what would make this false' required items.

findings.title: Canonical spec modified without explicit PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG cross-reference
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md Document Authority Model designates PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md as the 'reality/failure/proof log' and the canonical spec as 'normative requirements/roadmap'. Commit 8c7860f modifies 428 lines of the canonical spec to align with the Y9-2 family schema but there is no corresponding PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md entry for this doc change, nor any entry linking the schema alignment to a proof event. AGENTS.md states agents must not treat worksheets as authority and requires canonical docs to stay aligned with reality. Without a log entry, code state, proof state, and doc state cannot be independently verified against each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md entry for the 8c7860f canonical spec update. Per Anti-Overclaiming Contract, state what the spec change strictly documents, what it only anticipates, what is assumed, and what would make it incorrect. Label the update as 'WIRED' or 'PLANNED' (not PROVEN) if the Y9-2 schema is not yet verified via a UI-driven acceptance path.
evidence: CLAUDE.md §Document Authority Model: 'PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md — reality/failure/proof log' and 'docs/plans/2026-03-23-workbench-canonical-spec.md — normative requirements / roadmap / bug-priority / policy'. Both are canonical authority docs and changes to either should be traceable to the other.

CLAUDE.md §Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'Separate code state, proof state, and canon/doc state. Do not collapse them.' Commit 8c7860f changes 319 lines of canon without a corresponding proof-log entry documenting what is now claimed proven versus planned.

residual_risks: The compatibility alias `spec['family'] = filename_prefix` in service.py _normalize_template_action_spec (diff line ~462) is noted as deferred cleanup ('Step 11 will delete...'). If Step 11 is never executed, the legacy reader at service.py load_template_registry (post-normalization loop using `act.get('family', '')`) will silently continue to work via the alias rather than failing, masking any future registry that omits filename_prefix.

test_templates_api_exposes_normalized_contract uses a Flask test client to call /api/workbench/templates. If this test result is ever cited in PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md as acceptance evidence (rather than structural-contract evidence), it would constitute a process violation per AGENTS.md §Acceptance vs Diagnostic Enforcement. The test itself does not self-label its tier.

The review context states '25 tests pass' as a completion signal. CLAUDE.md prohibits inferring closure from green local behavior alone. If that count is ever cited in a canon or log entry without the four-part proof protocol, it would violate the Anti-Overclaiming Contract.
testing_gaps: No test covers the scenario where skin_family_scope entries in the registry are inconsistent with prefix_catalog entries for a non-human family. The green family in skin_family_scope has no entries in prefix_catalog, so cross-validation between the two structures is untested for non-human families.

The isTemplateActionAuthorable function in workbench.js is tested only indirectly via getEnabledActions. There are no unit tests for isTemplateActionAuthorable itself against edge cases: missing skin_family_scope on the registry, empty template_actions array on prefixSpec, or a templateSetKey not present in prefixSpec.template_actions.

The PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG entry for commit 31e142a describes tests that pass locally but does not record which environment (OS, Python version, Node version) or whether the test suite was run against the deployed Cloud Run instance. Verifier tests that depend on file system paths (e.g., test_template_registry_reference_paths_exist) would behave differently in a container environment.
